title: "Data Manipulation"
output: github_document

```{r, setup}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Load in the FAS Litters Data 
```{r}
litters_df = read_csv("./data/FAS_litters.csv", na = c("NA", ".", ""))
litters_df = janitor::clean_names(litters_df)
```

## 'Select'

Choose some columns and not others. 

```{r}
select(litters_df, gd0_weight:gd_of_birth)
```
```{r}
select(litters_df, -litter_number)
```
Remaining Columns....
```{r}
select(litters_df, GROUP=group, LITTer_NUmBer = litter_number)
```

```{r}
rename(litters_df, GROUP=group)
```

Select Helpers 

```{r}
select(litters_df, starts_with("gd"))
```
If you have a dataset for some key phrases, can select based on these 


```{r}
select(litters_df, litter_number, everything())
```
Move litter_number to the gront

```{r}
relocate(litters_df, litter_number)
```
Don't have to say everything in specific relocate


# "Filter'
Operates on rows, Select operates on columns

```{r}
filter(litters_df, gd0_weight < 22)
```
Filter rows where gestastional weight when mother found out pregnant less than 22

```{r}
filter(litters_df, gd_of_birth == 20)
```
two equal signs to ask a question is when gd is 20 not re-assign a variable 

```{r}
filter(litters_df, !(gd_of_birth == 20))
```
Not equal to gd_of_birth

```{r}
filter(litters_df, gd0_weight >=22, gd_of_birth == 20)
```

```{r}
filter(litters_df, group =="Con7")
```

```{r}
filter(litters_df, group %in% c("Con7", "Mod8"))
```
Either con7 or mod8
Real challenge is not using filter but understanding how to implement it using R


# 'Mutate'

```{r}
mutate(litters_df, 
       wt_gain = gd18_weight - gd0_weight, 
       group = str_to_lower(group))
```
